newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece gives Rifkind Cyprus proposals mixed review.
newsitem.headline: Greece gives Rifkind Cyprus proposals mixed review.

text.p: Greece gave a mixed response on Wednesday to a proposal by Britain's foreign minister Malcolm Rifkind aimed at getting peace talks underway on the divided Mediterranean island of Cyprus.

In a 10-point plan, Rifkind called on the island's rival Greek and Turkish communities to promote mutual trust as they edged towards peace and tried to create an internationally-recognised federal state.
British Foreign Secretary Rifkind presented his Cyprus proposals on Monday, saying they presented the best foundations for progress.
"There are positive and negative elements in Mr. Rifkind's proposals," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters.
He said Greece supported proposals of the internationally-recognised Cypriot government for a federation consisting of two communities under a single government.
"There should be freedom of communication and I am sure no one sees a solution to the Cyprus problem as long as a wall divides the island in two," Reppas said.

The United Nations have been trying to reunite the island as a federation for decades without success. Cyprus has been divided by barbed wire since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a coup engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.
Tension has increased perceptibly on the island in the past six months after the deaths of four people in ceasefire line incidents and both sides continue to build up their defences.
A Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in the north is recognised only by Ankara, which keeps 35,000 Turkish troops there.
The 11,500-strong Greek Cypriot national guard is weaker both in military hardware and personnel, but is engaged in a comprehensive programme to upgrade its defences.
Rifkind described the level of militarisation as "absurdly high and dangerously high".
